quotes.text: Azure isn't hard because the individual pieces are complicated because most of them aren't. It gets hard because the pieces multiply and multiplication without structure turns into noise.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the real root cause of Azure sprawl in one memorable line.

quotes.text: You might think more subscriptions means more control, but the opposite is true because more subscriptions means more places for the rules to drift.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Counters a common assumption about subscriptions and control.

quotes.text: A management group exists to group subscriptions that need the same rules not to draw a picture of your company.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear design rule against mirroring the org chart.

quotes.text: The difference between the two is the whole point. RBac is about who can act, and policy is about what is allowed to exist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisp distinction between RBAC and Azure Policy.

quotes.text: The subscription is where a charge is anchored, and the management group is where the view adds up. One is the bill and the other is the report.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable way to explain cost roll-up across the hierarchy.

takeaways: Subscriptions carry billing, quotas and the link to one Microsoft Entra tenant, while management groups sit above them purely for governance.
Access (RBAC) and Azure Policy assigned at a management group are inherited by every subscription and resource below it, and a deny higher up cannot be overridden lower down.
Follow the landing zone pattern: keep the hierarchy flat with platform, landing zones, sandbox and decommissioned branches, and use management group views to roll up usage costs.
hook: Once an Azure tenant grows past a handful of subscriptions, permissions, policies and costs drift out of control. This Simply Explained episode is for admins and cloud teams who need a clear map of the Azure hierarchy. It shows how management groups and subscriptions work together so you can set rules once and see costs in one place.
